score.note: First structural draft, evidence-guided from the family-transplant workspace's m2c decompile of the target's own retained bytes (out/family-transplants/main-080cb4ec/m2c/080cb4ec.c) plus the closest exact templates: games/gs1/src/battle/effects/puff_arc/run.c (structural template, score 8362/10000) and the already-adopted games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c (same 0x03001eec work-block family, and the source of the two-callback DrawRectangleFn[2]/rectangle_slot idiom this owner also uses). Initial draft measured candidate=760/reference=780/differing_halfwords=336/wrong_instructions=298, with the entire residual traceable to a single register-class swap: this compiler's allocator put the shared work pointer in r9 and the loop-index counters in fp/r6 (inconsistently between the two loops), where the reference keeps work in fp for the whole function and shares r9 between both loop counters. Fix 1: unifying the two loops' counter/pointer locals (previously separate 'i'/'p' for the 64-particle init loop and 'slot'/'cur' for the per-frame 16-particle draw loop) into one function-scope pair reused by both loops flipped the allocation to match the reference exactly for 'work' (fp) and the counters (r9) -- confirmed via --align (`mov fp, r2` / `add r5, fp` / `mov r1, fp` now byte-identical) -- dropping wrong_instructions 298->282. Fix 2: the piecewise drift-bucket chain (thresholds 0x2B/0x33/0x3B/0x43, mapping to bucket 3/2/1/0) was compiling to a 'default-then-ble-skip' shape when written through a local 'bucket' variable, versus the reference's 'bgt-then-set-then-b-to-merge' shape; writing directly to the struct field in each branch (`p->vel_x = 3;` etc, no local temp) reproduced the reference's exact branch topology and byte offsets for that chain, and applying the same 'write to the field, then a separate follow-up statement' shape to the negative sub-chain (v<=0x4B/0x53, bucket -1/-2/-3, written as `p->vel_x = 1/2/3; p->vel_x = -p->vel_x;` instead of `bucket = -mag`) further dropped differing_halfwords 319->302 (candidate grew 780->788, wrong_instructions rose 262->272, but differing_halfwords is the decisive metric per CONTRIBUTING and this shape scores strictly better on it; tried the exact-same-780-byte 262/319 variant too and kept the smaller differing_halfwords instead). Eight further experiments targeting the remaining large single mismatch -- an 8-byte-swapped stack layout where the reference places the two-callback `rectangle[2]` array at sp+16 and the `struct EffectPosition pos` scratch at sp+24, while this compiler's build places them the other way around -- all measured zero effect: declaration order (pos-before-rectangle and after), block-scoping pos narrowly vs at function scope, member_orbit's exact 'second_rectangle' intermediate-variable idiom for the second array slot, and indexing the draw callback through the bare `rectangle` array instead of a separate `rectangle_slot` pointer alias. This swap (and its knock-on low-register reshuffling inside the per-frame draw loop, plus small instruction-scheduling reorderings for a couple of independent immediate loads) accounts for effectively all of the remaining diff; every value, branch condition, branch target, call target, and constant in the function now matches the reference exactly under --align. This is the same class of compiler-internal, source-shape-insensitive register/stack-layout residual documented in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.json's sl/r9 finding for a sibling of the same family, and is not chased further per the project's ban on hand-forcing register assignment and its guidance against open-ended permutation search once independent structural levers stop moving the score.

Also reuses member_orbit's literal `heap_cache = (void **)0x03001EEC; cursor = heap_cache; work = *cursor++; canvas = *cursor;` cursor-advance idiom (matches this owner's `ldmia r3!, {r2}` exactly), and its Func_08002dd8(47) before Func_08002dd8(46) unload order at the tail.

For the negative drift-bucket sub-chain, writing the final value directly as `p->vel_x = -1/-2/-3` in each leaf (dropping the shared positive-then-negate step entirely): regressed relative to the kept form (candidate grew to 784, differing_halfwords rose to 328), because it lost the reference's single shared `negs` instruction; reverted in favor of `p->vel_x = 1/2/3; p->vel_x = -p->vel_x;`.

Using a local `mag` variable and writing `p->vel_x = mag; p->vel_x = -p->vel_x;` (instead of writing 1/2/3 directly to the field before negating): compiled identically to the plain `p->vel_x = -mag;` single-statement form (store-forwarding collapses it either way), so it did not reproduce the reference's separate materialize/negate shape the way direct field writes did; the kept version omits the intermediate local entirely.

Nested-if (nesting nested `if (v > threshold) { ... } else { bucket = N; }`) versus if-else-if chain phrasing for the same piecewise thresholds: byte-identical compiled output either way, confirming this compiler's front end normalizes both forms identically and the branch-shape fix came specifically from removing the local temp, not from the chain's surface syntax.

Semantic summary: republishes the caller's Efx* at work+0x7828, plays a start-up cue, sets BG2PA=0x0100 (affine identity scale) and BLDALPHA=0x1000, loads two draw-rectangle routines (heap kinds 46 and 47), decompresses a resource into the work block, zeroes two per-effect counters, schedules its own per-frame self-tick callback at 0x080CD261, derives a BG2X center offset from EffectPosition_ApplyStepAndYOffset(actors[0], ...), then seeds a 64-entry particle array (work+0x7080, 28 bytes/entry) with randomized fixed-point positions and a signed drift-velocity bucket (-3..3) selected by a piecewise range test on the random draw. Plays another cue, then runs 120 frames: a 16/17-frame linear BLDALPHA fade in at the start and a matching fade out over the last 16 frames (with a one-shot BLDCNT toggle at each fade's inner edge), a per-frame draw pass over the first 16 of the 64 particles (walked back to front) that selects one of the two heap-kind draw routines by the sign of each particle's drift velocity, looks its |bucket| up in a private 4-entry width/height/source-offset table, advances the particle's fixed-point position by its drift velocity once its staggered opening window is passed, or -- once a second, later per-particle threshold is passed -- keeps drawing it with height reduced by 4 instead of moving it (a fade/settle tail), a periodic (every 4th frame in [23,87], every 8th also cueing audio 0x85) ObjectGroup_UpdateMembers(actors[0], 7, 5, 0, 2) call that also arms the shared camera-shake counter at work+0x77A8, and an unconditional Camera_ApplyShake(8, 8) every frame. Tears down by unscheduling the self-tick callback and releasing both heap-kind draw routines (47 then 46, matching member_orbit's order) before a final opaque `Func_080cdbc0()` cleanup call shared with the template.

Every call target, branch condition, branch target displacement, and literal constant in the function now matches the reference exactly under `candidate-show --align`; the entire remaining 302-halfword residual is a single stack-layout swap (the rectangle[2] array and the EffectPosition scratch trade sp+16/sp+24) plus that swap's knock-on low-register reshuffling inside the per-frame draw loop and a few independent-instruction scheduling reorderings elsewhere -- no open semantic question remains.
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
